raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`download-rust-ext` always restores `rust-ext-x86_64-cp312`. Jobs with no same-run artifact (`/rerun-test`, or re-runs after the artifact expires) get x86 modules on GB300 and rebuild the Rust extensions from source: install takes ~6 min instead of ~30 s.

```
cache_key_prefix: rust-ext-x86_64-cp312
Cache hit for: rust-ext-x86_64-cp312-44722fe8...
::warning::no prebuilt Rust extension .cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so for: server grpc multimodal mem_cache mem_cache_inspection; building from source
Prepared 1 package in 5m 55s
```

The aarch64 entries already exist on main (`rust-ext-aarch64-cp312-<same hash>`, seeded by `pr-test.yml` / `seed-rust-ext-cache.yml`).

## Modifications

Restore with `rust-ext-aarch64-cp312` on ARM64 runners. x86 behavior and the prefix lint are unchanged.

files.patch:
@@ -11,7 +11,7 @@ inputs:
     required: false
     default: ''
   cache_key_prefix:
-    description: 'Must match what _pr-test-rust-ext-build.yml saves under.'
+    description: 'Must match what _pr-test-rust-ext-build.yml saves under. ARM64 runners always restore rust-ext-aarch64-cp312.'
     required: false
     default: rust-ext-x86_64-cp312
 
@@ -53,7 +53,7 @@ runs:
         path: |
           python/sglang/srt/rust_extensions/_*.so
           python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/rust_tree_core/mem_cache*.so
-        key: ${{ inputs.cache_key_prefix }}-${{ hashFiles('rust/**', 'proto/**', 'python/setup.py', 'python/pyproject.toml', 'python/sglang/srt/rust_extensions/torch_build.py', '.github/workflows/_pr-test-rust-ext-build.yml', 'scripts/ci/utils/stage_rust_ext_modules.sh') }}
+        key: ${{ runner.arch == 'ARM64' && 'rust-ext-aarch64-cp312' || inputs.cache_key_prefix }}-${{ hashFiles('rust/**', 'proto/**', 'python/setup.py', 'python/pyproject.toml', 'python/sglang/srt/rust_extensions/torch_build.py', '.github/workflows/_pr-test-rust-ext-build.yml', 'scripts/ci/utils/stage_rust_ext_modules.sh') }}
 
     # Job-wide, but only setup.py reads it, and only while building.
     # Whether the modules suit this interpreter is not decided here:
